summary: Independent review of TASK-078 (REQ-104 hygiene: delete orphan IPC command commands::sync_now + revise four stale 'Miniflux fallback' comments). Candidate binding: recomputed sha256 for all 160 candidate_files - 160/160 match, 0 mismatch, 0 missing. Scope: exactly 5 non-.workflow-kit files modified, all inside allowed_paths; git diff numstat is 0/9 (commands/sync.rs), 0/1 (lib.rs), 1/1 (staged_refresh_e2e.rs), 3/2 (sync_phases_e2e.rs), 2/2 (types.ts) - pure deletion plus comment text, and a filtered diff for assert/SELECT/expect/== lines returns empty, so no assertion, SQL, threshold or logic changed. (1) commands::sync_now is genuinely orphaned: git grep for 'sync_now' over src/ (exit 1), tools/ (exit 1) and every *.json/*.toml/*.yml (no matches) is empty; the only in-tree survivors are the doc mention at sync/mod.rs:25 and the core function sync::sync_now at sync/phases.rs:82, which is KEPT and still called by sync_e2e.rs:96,161,200,257,287, dual_client_e2e.rs:210,236,262,274,337 and fever_sync_live_e2e.rs:46. The frontend's real entry is api.syncPhase -> inv('sync_phase', {which, full}) at src/lib/api.ts:510, called from src/store/slices/sync.ts:79,86 and src/components/settings/SyncTab.tsx:92,98; 'syncNow' appears nowhere. No IPC-legal name is lost. (2) Comment accuracy - all four revised sites checked clause by clause against code and history, and all hold: fetch_failed is written only by set_feed_fetch_state (db/feeds.rs:115-139, reached from the NotModified, Body and Err branches of ingestion.rs at :383/:398/:487), has no other Rust reader, and its consumers are exactly the frontend error badge (api.ts:553 fetchFailed -> Sidebar.tsx:240) and the fail_count/next_retry_at backoff consumed by feeds_due_for_refresh (db/feeds.rs:146-160); source='miniflux' has exactly one writer, upsert_remote_entry at sync/entries.rs:214 (doc at :169) reached from merge_pulled_entry's None branch (:145-152), while source='direct' comes only from the staged ingestion pipeline (ingestion.rs:302); and origin really is neutralised - it can only be 'local' (migrations.rs:172) or 'remote' (:224 UPDATE feeds SET origin='remote' WHERE origin='miniflux'), so 'miniflux' is not a valid origin value and the new 'unrelated to the feed's origin' clause is correct. The historical claim 'removed at 0ba940f' is TRUE and verified rather than an unverifiable absolute: at 0ba940f^ sync.rs:584 has 'let (since_s, miniflux_feeds, failed_feeds)' and :606 'for feed in &failed_feeds' pulling via feeds_fetch_failed_bound (:589), while at 0ba940f itself the same grep returns only the function definitions at db.rs:603/627 with no caller. No new never/always/only absolute, no mechanism attributed to the wrong field, and no inconsistency between the two comments. (3) Mutation test of the classic half-deletion state: restoring only the lib.rs registration line while the function stays deleted fails to compile (error[E0433] for commands::__cmd__sync_now and __tauri_command_name_sync_now in lib.rs, exit 101), so the pair cannot be half-reverted silently; lib.rs was then restored byte-identically (sha256 3950b80eb66ab38e7b949ce7bf1e5bb66e53512dfbe7891c6b70865f6ab6021d) and re-verified against the packet. (4) Regression: recomputing the totals from the raw logs gives cargo 193 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored, identical to the TASK-077 baseline RUN-f5c07ebc (193/0/9); lint 0 warnings / 0 errors exit 0; build exit 0 with empty stderr; frontend 303/303. I independently re-ran cargo build (exit 0, only the pre-existing linker_messages warning), cargo test --lib (95 passed / 0 failed, exit 0) and npm run test:frontend (303/303, exit 0). No new dead_code/unused warning: the warning-line multiset of the candidate cargo_test stderr is identical to the baseline's (15 lines each), and every never-used item is a helper in tests/mock_greader.rs, unrelated to the deletion. No dependency change (package.json / package-lock.json / Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock diff empty), all five files LF-only with a trailing newline, and the real user database is untouched (fluxreader.db 90112 bytes, mtime 2026-09-18T17:58:09Z, sha256 419b118e050a08c2..., the same value recorded before this task). No real defect found, so the verdict is PASS with no findings. Two residual stale Miniflux-era comments were found in nearby lines of files this task edited (sync_phases_e2e.rs:213 cites the Miniflux REST endpoint 'GET /v1/entries/ids?status=unread', which no longer exists in the code - the GReader reconcile uses fetch_stream_ids on the read/starred streams; and types.ts:5 still says 'Miniflux feed and category structures are identical'). Both are pre-existing, were not among the four sites handed over by TASK-070, and are not claims this task introduced; they are recorded as observations under maintainability for a possible follow-up, not as defects of this candidate.

review_checks.analysis: Both acceptance criteria are met, verified against the code rather than the author's narrative. (1) 'commands::sync_now and its lib.rs registration are both gone' - git diff shows the function body plus its doc comment removed from src-tauri/src/commands/sync.rs (9 lines) and the single registration line removed from src-tauri/src/lib.rs (1 line, between commands::sync_local_feeds and commands::sync_status); the current generate_handler list at lib.rs:246-262 no longer contains sync_now. No product caller depends on the invoke name: git grep 'sync_now' over src/ and tools/ exits 1 (empty), over src-tauri/src finds only sync/mod.rs:25 (a doc line) and sync/phases.rs:82 (the core function), and a grep over all *.json (including tauri.conf.json and capabilities/default.json, which holds only plugin permissions) returns no match. 'syncNow' is gone everywhere. The frontend's full-sync entry is api.syncPhase -> inv('sync_phase') at api.ts:510, unchanged, called at store/slices/sync.ts:79,86 and settings/SyncTab.tsx:92,98. Critically, the core function sync::sync_now that had to survive is intact at src-tauri/src/sync/phases.rs:82-92 (feeds_phase then states_phase(full=true), same report merge) and is still called directly by sync_e2e.rs (5 sites), dual_client_e2e.rs (5 sites) and fever_sync_live_e2e.rs:46 - only the commands-layer wrapper was removed. (2) 'the stale Miniflux-fallback comments are corrected to current fetch_failed semantics' - four sites were revised, a superset of the three enumerated in the objective (types.ts:70 and sync_phases_e2e.rs:284 were added within the same allowed files, same defect class, and are disclosed in the change artifact). All four are accurate: types.ts:45 now says the flag drives the frontend error indicator plus exponential backoff, matching the only writer set_feed_fetch_state (db/feeds.rs:125-134) and the only readers (FeedRow -> api.ts:553 -> Sidebar.tsx:240; feeds_due_for_refresh filtering on next_retry_at at db/feeds.rs:155); types.ts:70 now describes direct as client direct fetching (ingestion.rs:302) and miniflux as 'pulled via the sync backend' (sole writer sync/entries.rs:214), explicitly as a historical name that is protocol-neutralised; staged_refresh_e2e.rs:195 now names the real consumers; sync_phases_e2e.rs:246-248 keeps the historically true root cause and adds the removal commit. No behaviour was changed alongside the text. The change set stays inside allowed_paths - the 5 modified non-.workflow-kit paths are exactly the objective's files (src/lib/api.ts is in allowed_paths but was not needed and is untouched), and no file was added, renamed or left untracked outside .workflow-kit.

The recorded numbers reproduce from the raw logs, and I re-ran the cheap gates myself. Summing every 'test result:' line of RUN-6aeb3b77f8984b48ad8c1905007b6c5f-cargo_test.stdout.txt gives 193 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored; the same computation on the TASK-077 baseline log RUN-f5c07ebc890b4519a2f79d843e8d2bcd-cargo_test.stdout.txt gives the identical 193/0/9, so the deletion cost no covered assertion and the '>=193, 0 failed, 9 ignored unchanged' criterion holds. lint log: 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors' with exit 0. build log: Vite assets emitted, stderr empty, exit 0 (I did not rerun npm run build, per instruction; the typecheck side is covered by cargo build and the frontend suite both staying green). frontend log ends with '303/303' and exit 0. Independently executed: cargo build -> exit 0 with exactly one warning, the pre-existing 'linker stdout' linker_messages warning; cargo test --lib -> 95 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored, exit 0; npm run test:frontend -> 303/303, exit 0. No new dead_code or unused warnings from the deletion (the classic risk of removing a registered item): the state is fine because the function and its registration were removed together, and I confirmed by mutation that removing only one side does not compile. As a warning-level cross-check I diffed the multiset of warning lines of the candidate cargo_test stderr against the baseline's - identical, 15 lines each; every never-used item is a test helper in tests/mock_greader.rs (set_greader_api_prefix, set_fail_edit_tag, ...), present in the baseline and untouched by this diff. Assertions are provably untouched: git diff --numstat is 0/9, 0/1, 1/1, 3/2, 2/2 (no added lines outside comment text), and a diff filtered for assert/SELECT/expect/== lines returns nothing. No new dependencies (git diff HEAD -- package.json package-lock.json src-tauri/Cargo.toml src-tauri/Cargo.lock is empty); the five changed files are LF-only with a trailing newline; the real user database was not written (90112 bytes, mtime 2026-09-18T17:58:09Z, sha256 419b118e050a08c2..., unchanged since before this task; all test databases are tempfile-based).

For a deletion task the failure path to hunt is a still-reachable reference to the removed symbol, including string-level and IPC-name references, plus the half-deleted state. (a) String/IPC level: the invoke name 'sync_now' does not appear in src/, tools/, any JSON/TOML/YAML/config, or the Tauri capability manifest (capabilities/default.json contains only core/plugin permissions, so the command was never declared there either); the only occurrences in Rust are the core function definition and one doc line. Because Tauri dispatches commands by name from the webview and no webview code sends that name, no runtime path can now fail with 'command not found'. Removing a registered-but-uncalled command also cannot change any error, empty or repeated execution: the wrapper's whole body was a single delegation to the identical core function, so even a hypothetical stale caller would have produced the same result through sync_phase. (b) Half-deletion mutation, executed and then fully reverted: I restored only the lib.rs registration line (backing the file up first) with the function still deleted; cargo build failed with error[E0433] 'cannot find __cmd__sync_now / __tauri_command_name_sync_now in commands' in src/lib.rs, exit 101. So the most likely partial-deletion defect is caught at compile time and cannot ship. The file was then restored byte-identically (sha256 3950b80eb66ab38e7b949ce7bf1e5bb66e53512dfbe7891c6b70865f6ab6021d, re-checked against the packet's candidate hash) and the backup deleted. (c) Data and DB boundary: nothing in the diff touches schema or queries - fetch_failed, fail_count and next_retry_at keep their writer (db/feeds.rs:115-139) and their consumers, so the fetch-failure and backoff paths still behave as the tests expect; migrations are unmodified, so existing databases remain compatible. (d) Coverage of the retained core path: the integration tests that guard the sync merge and backoff behaviour (sync_e2e, dual_client_e2e, sync_phases_e2e, scheduler_e2e, fever_sync_live_e2e) all still call sync::sync_now or the phase functions and all pass; the 9 ignored network/live tests are unchanged in count.

The change reduces surface and removes misleading documentation without adding abstraction, dependency or duplication. Deleting commands::sync_now removes a second invoke name reaching the same core logic as sync_phase (the wrapper was a one-line delegation to sync::sync_now, so two IPC entry points exposed one behaviour with two argument shapes); the live entry (sync_phase with its which selector) is untouched. The four comment revisions replace claims about a mechanism that no longer exists with descriptions that match the code, and the sync_phases_e2e.rs rewrite deliberately keeps the historical narration but pins it to the commit that ended the mechanism - the failure mode that cost three review rounds on sibling TASK-070 (a false 'never implemented' absolute) is avoided: I verified the cited commit 0ba940f really is the removal point (caller present at 0ba940f^ sync.rs:589, absent at 0ba940f) and that no new unverifiable absolute was introduced. Comment and code now agree in all four sites and with the neighbouring sync/mod.rs:7-15 and ingestion.rs:4-7 assertions from TASK-070. Dependency direction is unchanged: the commands layer keeps only the commands it still serves, and the sync layer's public surface (phases.rs:82 sync_now) is intact for both command and test callers. Residual staleness observed but not charged to this candidate, since it is pre-existing and outside the four sites handed over by TASK-070: (i) src-tauri/tests/sync_phases_e2e.rs:213 still names the Miniflux REST endpoint 'GET /v1/entries/ids?status=unread' as the mechanism of the light-sync reconcile, but no such path exists in the code (grep for 'v1/entries' returns nothing; the GReader implementation reconciles via fetch_stream_ids on the read/starred streams at greader_pull.rs:117-125), and it sits about 30 lines above the comment this task edited in the same file; (ii) src/types.ts:5 still says 'Miniflux feed and category structures are identical' in the module header of the same file whose two comments were corrected; (iii) src-tauri/tests/sync_content_e2e.rs:2 and src-tauri/tests/sync_gap_repro_e2e.rs keep Miniflux-era wording in files outside allowed_paths. Items (i) and (ii) are inside allowed paths and would be the natural next hygiene increment for REQ-104; they are not regressions and not claims introduced here, and the change artifact explicitly asked reviewers to report such residue rather than asserting none remains. One traceability note: acceptance criterion 2 speaks of 'three' comment sites while four were revised, and two of them concern the source field rather than fetch_failed; the delivered work is a disclosed superset of the criterion's intent (replace stale Miniflux-fallback semantics with accurate current ones), so this is a wording mismatch in the criterion, not missing or extra behaviour.

No performance effect exists to measure, and I claim none. The change deletes an IPC wrapper that had zero callers and edits comment text, so it removes no executed instruction from any workload: commands::sync_now was never invoked (no frontend caller, no string reference anywhere), and its body was a single delegation to sync::sync_now, which is retained verbatim at src-tauri/src/sync/phases.rs:82-92 (feeds_phase then states_phase(full=true), the same report merge). The hot path that actually determines sync and refresh cost is untouched: the live entry api.syncPhase -> inv('sync_phase') -> feeds_phase/states_phase, the batch sync_match_maps prefetch with O(1) map lookups in the merge loop, the staged fetch pipeline, and the scheduler's feeds_due_for_refresh/feeds_all_ids queries are all byte-identical. No SQL, index, threshold or loop changed (git diff numstat shows no non-comment added lines), and no dependency was added or removed, so bundle size and compile inputs are unchanged; cargo build finished in 0.42s with exit 0 on the candidate. The quality goal's performance targets (ten-thousand-item startup, layout switching, social-layout article loading) belong to REQ-001/003 and are not on this deletion surface, and no workload or baseline for them was defined here, so no benchmark was fabricated. Method note: this is a static scope judgement over the diff and the unchanged call graph, not a measurement; no timing comparison was performed or is possible for a never-called function.
